summary: Unexpected rate limit spike causing 429s for bulk embedding job
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightPath Analytics observed a sudden increase in 429 rate-limit errors during a scheduled bulk embeddings job between 02:10-02:37 UTC on 2026-03-10. The job processes ~15M text segments nightly.

Impact:
- Multiple customers using the same public API key (shared SaaS workload) experienced transient 429s and retries, causing the BrightPath job to stretch from its normal 25 minutes to ~3 hours.
- No data loss reported; retries completed but with degraded throughput and higher cost.

Environment:
- prod-us-east
- API: /v1/embeddings (hosted public API)
- Customer tier: self_serve (BrightPath)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Kick off large multi-threaded embedding job (15M text segments) using our public API key and default concurrency.
2. After ~5k requests, clients start receiving intermittent 429 responses.
3. Client-side retry logic succeeds but with exponential backoff, dramatically increasing overall run time.

Relevant logs & metrics:
- Spike in 429s visible on token-level and route-level dashboards starting 02:10 UTC (correlates to a short latency increase on api-gateway).
- Route rate limiter logs show a surge of allowed burst requests then enforcement; a small percentage of requests hit per-account rate limits before the global rate limiting enforcement stabilized.
- No corresponding spike in CPU/GPU of serving-runtime nodes; autoscaling did not trigger.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: a misconfigured burst window in the API gateway combined with an unusual traffic burst pattern from a handful of high-concurrency clients.
- Related config: recent gatekeeper change (K8s configmap) rolled 2026-03-09 adjusted per-route burst thresholds for embeddings-route.
- Correlated with a scheduled third-party ingest that started at 02:05 UTC from BrightPath; their job concurrency briefly exceeded expected limits.
- Observed that token-bucket refill rates applied per-route and per-account had overlapping enforcement which caused an oscillation when many clients retried simultaneously.

Workaround applied:
- Temporarily raised per-account burst allowance for embeddings-route for affected customers (BrightPath + two similar accounts) at 03:00 UTC, which reduced 429s and allowed the jobs to complete.
- Enabled a short-lived adaptive backoff on the API gateway to smooth retry storms.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short term: keep elevated per-account burst allowance for 24 hours while we complete a root-cause analysis.
- Medium term: introduce a jittered retry guidance and client-side SDK update to spread retries, plus a soft-queue on the gateway to absorb retry storms.
- Long term: rework rate-limiter coordination between per-account and per-route token buckets to avoid oscillatory enforcement under large concurrent retries.

Related artifacts:
- Related GitHub experiment PR: pr-4217-experiment-adaptive-batching-simulator (used for load modeling).
- Confluence runbook referenced: CON-8234-embedding-route-rate-limiting (link: https://confluence.internal/CON-8234).
